reading.body:
The Flexential Raleigh facility in Morrisville, North Carolina publishes 4.31 MW of critical load UPS capacity across approximately 100,000 square feet, making it the second-largest facility by power in the state among those with disclosed figures.

At a typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, this capacity would support roughly 100 racks. The published power figure does not specify current occupancy or workload type, so it cannot be confirmed whether this infrastructure is currently serving AI deployments or capable of doing so. The facility holds multiple compliance certifications including PCI DSS, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, and HITRUST, which qualify it for regulated workloads but do not indicate AI-specific capabilities or constraints.

North Carolina has 19 mapped data center facilities statewide, but only five publish power capacity data. Flexential Raleigh accounts for 8.6 percent of the state's 50.3 MW of disclosed critical IT load. This modest share means the facility alone does not reflect regional grid strain or emerging AI infrastructure density. The overall picture in North Carolina remains incomplete because fourteen facilities do not publish their power figures.
